segments.words: What was the work like that you did?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Well, it was a waiting table. We'd go to work at 5 .30 in the morning, and then we'd... Breakfast at 6. Breakfast at 6. He had to go on to work at 5. Well, Mr. Thomas and his wife had there, had things pretty well, you know.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: And then, he had the eggs and stuff, and I just had to put the coffee and the big coffee pots on the table and carry the food in, because I'd set the table. segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: You worked about three shifts, right?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan

And then once a week, why, we scrubbed the floor with lye and a broom, you know, and throw buckets of water on it to rinse all the stuff off, because, you know, it had to keep it. They would have one bit of talking at the table. They came in at eight and left. They never talked or anything. I don't know whether it was some custom that they had developed or what, but they'd come in and eat and go. And in 10, 15 minutes, everybody would be gone. And you'd clean it all up again. Yeah. But let's say you work seven days a week, you know, with hardware. But you got $60 a month. Board room. Board room. And that was a lot of money on those days. segments.words: They never... even if they... I've heard that they would drink quite a bit even up in the... you know. They didn't do as much drinking in camp. No, not in camp. Oh, no, no, no, no, nothing like that. And they both had their delivery. They both had delivery. You'd just call up and ask what you want, and you'd get it delivered, you know. Horse and buggy.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: So people didn't have to go to town and carry anything. Of course, as I say, that was before everybody had cars, you know. And both our brothers were delivery boys at times. And my brother Dee, that's Dee Dee's dad, you know, used to deliver them. They had to take care of the horses and everything, you know. And he was just a kid, I don't think, you know, and... 12, 13 when he was doing that.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: That was before I worked down there.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: How long would that store be used during the day, do you remember?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Well, I don't think their hours were much different than they were. I think when I worked there, I worked from 9 to 6. And a couple nights a week. I think it was only one night they stayed open late.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: Saturday night, wasn't it?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Saturday night when the lumberjacks came to town and everything.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: Is that when a lot of lumberjacks would they show up to?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Yeah. That was their only time they could to buy, you know. No, I don't think their hours weren't any different than they are right now, or even...

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: Do you remember some of the people like Pat Malone?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Oh, I should have said so. He was a real character. He was just part of the town. He was a great person. He was just part of everybody's family, I think. He was so kind and good to everybody.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: I heard he was really good to kids. He was just one of those children.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: I don't care how big they were. They were all kids in his eyes, you know what I mean?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Like the older boys, me 17, 18, he was nice to them. He was good to the little kids. And I can just close my eyes and see him yet. I can too, and I can see him at night. He used to say he'd get going real fast. It was like days and everybody used to say, well, Pat's got a clue. Got a clue. Pat's got a clue. He's gone. He walks so fast. Well, I think he was great for the town of old. I think he was real good. I can still see him, young Dave Ellison, sitting in the room.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Yeah, well, Pat was a real nice old man. I say there's probably a lot of others that we remember.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: If we could just think of him, you know?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: It was Billy O 'Mara. He was a nice, he was real good too.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Wasn't that type?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: No, he wasn't that type. He just worked in the city right back here. Oh, not yet.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Haven't you? Not many of the Davids left, is there?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: I think Mary and Henry are the only ones.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: They live in Lewiston, don't they?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: But I thought maybe...

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Do they live in Lewiston?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Yeah. Mary and Henry, they don't know.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: They could probably give you a lot of... He could, because he worked on the trains and everything.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: He worked on the trains with Dad, didn't he?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Breaking or something.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryanrager
segments.words: And have you talked to any of the Hayses?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: They lived up there in Portland a long time.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Georgia O'Keeffe was a Hays. She would probably just be able to give you a lot of information. She lives in Seattle someplace, and I don't know. But she has... Bob Denimann, I think, lives in Lewiston, or... He lives in Lewiston. Lives in Lewiston.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: What's his name?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Bob Denimann. And this would be his mother-in-law. I don't know what her name is now. I don't either, should she remember.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: But she could probably give you a lot of information, because she was there, so she was just a girdle.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: I don't know. Give me your words.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: We're living in a same house, we're in a carnival.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: I don't think we're being much help to you.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: It's hard for me to concentrate with somebody.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: I know the microphone you're taping like this. The microphone is going to pick up the kid so loud.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: Oh, is that right?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: It's going to pick up the baby. Oh, I never thought of it.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: Picks up noises like that. It's sort of annoying because it picks up. It picks up, I mean, that's a sharp noise. And it just, you know, we can block it out, and we don't even hear it very much. But the mic will just, you know, if you go like this, it'll ground up.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: Is that a mechanical noise like that?

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: It'll, you know, it really picks up loud. Hmm.

segments.speaker: Viola White Cameron or Grace Ryan
segments.words: It's bad.

segments.speaker: Laura Schrager
segments.words: Yeah, we probably should have at one point gotten a better mic. We got it.
